glance: IgA nephropathy: four NEJM phase 3 reports (sibeprenlimab, atacicept, povetacicept, ravulizumab) plus iptacopan long-term data; eGFR slopes stabilized on APRIL-directed agents.
LEAP-Block (JAMA): left bundle-branch area pacing beat right ventricular pacing on a composite driven by heart failure events (2.4% vs 12.5%).
AGA/AASLD issued a primary biliary cholangitis guideline (6 recommendations; PPAR agonists and linerixibat now included).
PMR imaging recommendations: imaging is for intermediate pretest probability only; no single first-line modality.
Neutral or negative: 0/1 h vs 0/3 h troponin pathway (no length-of-stay gain), rituximab vs azathioprine in EGPA, efzofitimod in sarcoidosis, mitapivat pain crises.
Empagliflozin in ADPKD (pilot, n=50): faster total kidney volume growth than placebo; hypothesis-generating.

top.title: IgA nephropathy: four phase 3 reports in one week
bullets: Sibeprenlimab and atacicept final analyses add eGFR data: annualized slope about 0 vs -4.2 to -5.6 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr on placebo.
Povetacicept and ravulizumab are interim proteinuria analyses (UPCR down 52.0% and 46.6% vs 4.3% and 5.6%).
Iptacopan extension: proteinuria reduction sustained to 48 months.
top.caveat: All industry-funded; 24 to 104 weeks of follow-up; tiny event counts on composite end points; no standalone kidney failure data yet.

top.title: LEAP-Block: LBBAP vs right ventricular pacing (JAMA)
bullets: 499 patients, AV block, LVEF 50% or higher, expected pacing burden over 40%.
Primary composite at 24 months: 2.4% vs 12.5% (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.19-0.73).
HF events 3.4% vs 11.3%.
top.caveat: Driven by HF events; no significant difference in death, biventricular upgrade, or device complications. 14 Chinese centers.

top.title: AGA/AASLD guideline on primary biliary cholangitis
bullets: Suggests PBC-specific ANA when AMA-negative; UDCA first-line; liver stiffness for prognosis.
PPAR agonists for inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA; linerixibat for moderate-to-severe pruritus.
UDCA prophylaxis after liver transplantation.
top.caveat: Certainty of evidence moderate to very low. Published in both Gastroenterology and Hepatology.

guidelines.title: Management of primary biliary cholangitis
bullets: 6 GRADE-based recommendations; see Top 3.

guidelines.title: Imaging in polymyalgia rheumatica
bullets: 3 principles, 7 recommendations.
PMR remains a clinical diagnosis; imaging not needed to confirm (high probability) or exclude (low probability).
Most useful at intermediate pretest probability; no single first-line modality, individualize.

guidelines.title: Female-specific prevention and management of cardiovascular disease (scientific statement)
bullets: New Female Life Stage construct: perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause; pregnancy as a modifying event.
Crosswalks society guidance to reduce fragmentation across specialties.
Two companion AHA advisories the same week (PMID 42929148, 42929153).

guidelines.title: Anemia in cancer and CKD (position statement)
bullets: Consensus diagnostic approach and management.
Open questions flagged: iron, ESAs, transfusion thresholds, HIF-PH inhibitors in malignancy.

guidelines.issuer: Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases (practical recommendations)
guidelines.title: Revaccination after BCMA-targeted therapies in autoimmune disease
bullets: BCMA-directed therapy lowers vaccine-specific titres and total immunoglobulins.
Proposes pragmatic revaccination with minimal serologic monitoring; evidence extrapolated from oncology.

guidelines.title: Medical treatment of ulcerative colitis, 2026
bullets: GRADE-ADOLOPMENT adaptation of source guidelines.
Covers induction and maintenance, acute severe UC, surgery, biosimilars, subcutaneous formulations, sequencing.

guidelines.title: Medical treatment of Crohn's disease, 2026
bullets: Biologic and small-molecule positioning, combination therapy, de-escalation, biosimilar switching, perianal fistulizing disease.
Companion IBD diagnosis and monitoring guideline: PMID 42928004.

guidelines.title: Management of shift work disorder
bullets: All recommendations conditional.
Modafinil or armodafinil before the shift for sleepiness.
Bright light at night plus fixed daytime sleep plus reduced-light glasses for circadian adaptation (very low certainty).
No preference between 8-hour and 12-hour night shifts.

items.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA nephropathy, final analysis
bullets: eGFR slope 0.3 vs -4.2 mL/min/1.73 m2/yr (difference 4.5).
Composite kidney end point 0.4% vs 11.2%.

items.title: Atacicept in IgA nephropathy (ORIGIN 3), final efficacy
bullets: eGFR slope through week 104: -0.60 vs -5.60 (difference 5.00).
Composite progression 5.1% vs 17.8% (HR 0.24).
No atacicept patient reached dialysis, transplant, or death vs 7 on placebo.

items.title: Povetacicept in IgA nephropathy (RAINIER), interim
bullets: Efficacy in first 199 randomized (557 treated overall).
UPCR -52.0% vs -4.3% at week 36; hematuria resolution 85% vs 23%.
Serious AEs 3% vs 4%.

items.title: Ravulizumab in IgA nephropathy, interim
bullets: 485 randomized, 352 in interim analysis.
UPCR -46.6% vs -5.6% at week 34.
No meningococcal infections.
items.caveat: Surrogate end point; intravenous every 8 weeks.

items.title: Iptacopan long-term outcomes in IgA nephropathy
bullets: Up to 48 months: eGFR slope -3.49/yr; UPCR ratio to baseline 0.61, sustained.
Placebo-to-iptacopan switchers: slope improved from -5.29 to -2.11/yr.

items.title: Empagliflozin in ADPKD
bullets: n=50, 12 months; well tolerated.
Height-adjusted total kidney volume grew faster: 10.5%/yr vs 5.1%/yr.
eGFR dip of -6.2 at 1 month, then no difference in slope.
items.caveat: Small pilot; kidney volume signal is hypothesis-generating.

items.title: 0/1 h vs 0/3 h troponin pathways for suspected MI
bullets: No reduction in ED length of stay (ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.85-1.25).
Direct discharge 67.0% vs 65.8% (OR 1.31, 0.79-2.16).
Short-term adverse events low with both pathways.
items.caveat: Pooled safety estimate imprecise; I2 above 97% for several outcomes.

items.title: SGLT2 inhibitors and hemoglobin, hematocrit, iron markers
bullets: 85 RCTs, 70,543 participants.
Hemoglobin +0.60 g/dL, hematocrit +2.36% vs control.
EPO up, transferrin saturation down.
items.caveat: Authors state clinical significance is unclear.

items.title: SGLT2 inhibitors vs DPP-4 inhibitors, age 75 or older
bullets: 4,997 vs 1,289 initiators (British Columbia).
AKI HR 0.76 (0.60-0.95); all-cause hospitalization HR 0.87 (0.77-0.98).
No difference in infection, DKA, falls, fractures.
items.caveat: Observational; intervals for DKA, falls, fractures compatible with benefit or harm.

items.title: Semaglutide vs dulaglutide or liraglutide in hemodialysis
bullets: 1,312 vs 2,601 users (USRDS).
Mortality sHR 0.82 (0.70-0.97); hospitalization sHR 0.91 (0.83-0.99).
1-year weight loss 4.8% vs 3.4%.
Semaglutide vs liraglutide alone not significant.

items.title: Non-invasive tests in MASLD
bullets: 1,590 biopsy-confirmed patients, 13 countries; 12 single markers, 18 panels.
Advanced fibrosis AUC: SomaSignal 0.92, FibroMeter-VCTE 0.87, Agile 3+ 0.84.
Cirrhosis AUC: FibroMeter-VCTE 0.94.
Single markers weak for at-risk MASH; GGT-first two-step approaches met the 0.80 threshold.
items.caveat: Reference standard is centrally scored histology in a biopsy-confirmed cohort.

items.title: Saroglitazar in PBC after inadequate UDCA response (EPICS-III)
bullets: Phase 3 n=148.
Biochemical response at week 52: 56.7% vs 9.8%.
ALP normalization 8.2% vs 0%.
items.caveat: Biochemical surrogate; baseline ALP higher in the saroglitazar arm.

items.title: Rituximab vs azathioprine for EGPA maintenance
bullets: n=98 (France).
No difference in total remission duration over 28 months (P=.38); relapse 14.3% vs 18.4%.
Severe infections 46.9% vs 24.5%, mainly SARS-CoV-2.
items.caveat: Rituximab not superior; enrolment 2018-2022 overlapped COVID-19.

items.title: Autologous HSCT in systemic sclerosis, long-term
bullets: n=80, median follow-up 9.2 years.
Progression-free survival 81% / 72% / 60% at 2 / 5 / 10 years.
Treatment-related deaths 6%; 43% in remission off immunosuppression at 10 years.

items.title: Efzofitimod in pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT)
bullets: Three arms; primary end point was change in oral corticosteroid dose at week 48.
No reduction vs placebo; well tolerated.
Steroid taper alone reached lower doses in many patients.

items.title: Depemokimab (twice-yearly anti-IL-5) in eosinophilic asthma, 2-year data
bullets: 629 patients in the extension.
Exacerbation rate 0.51 (year 1) and 0.56 (year 2).
No treatment-related serious AEs; lung function and symptom gains maintained.

items.title: Cefepime-zidebactam for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections
bullets: 72 treated; 82.4% of qualifying isolates were MBL producers (mostly NDM).
Investigator-assessed clinical cure 91.7%; externally adjudicated 86.7%.

items.title: Duke criteria versions in suspected infective endocarditis
bullets: 3,448 suspected episodes, 38% adjudicated IE; possible IE stayed at 29-33%.
Sensitivity for definite IE: 63% (2015 Duke-ESC) to 74% (2023 ISCVID) and 71% (2023 ESC).
Specificity declined (72% to 59% in at least one newer version).
items.caveat: Two Swiss centers; reference standard is Endocarditis Team diagnosis.

items.title: Mitapivat in sickle cell disease (RISE UP)
bullets: Hemoglobin response 41% vs 3%.
Annualized pain crises 2.6 vs 3.1 (P=0.12, not significant).
Serious AEs 20% vs 29%.
items.caveat: Co-primary pain crisis end point missed; Agios-funded.

method: Source: PubMed E-utilities, entry date within the last 7 days. Query A: 30 internal medicine and subspecialty journals. Query B: publication type Practice Guideline or Guideline in internal medicine topics. Duplicates removed by PMID.
Screening and summaries: Claude, from abstracts and metadata only. Numbers are copied from abstracts; open the linked record before citing.
Full text: PMC records exist for 18 of 191 candidates. A PMC record does not guarantee machine-readable full text.
Excluded by scope: oncology (including ASCO living guidelines and NEJM lung and bladder trials), neurology and stroke, pediatrics, health policy, narrative and opinion pieces.
Not searched: preprints, society websites without PubMed indexing (ACC, ESC, KDIGO, IDSA, ADA living updates), FDA actions.
Badges describe the result against the primary end point: Positive, Negative, Neutral (no clear difference), Descriptive (observational, uncontrolled, or no efficacy test).
